title: Retail cannabis opt-out and Elora Rocks payment terms
subtitle: South Fergus Secondary Plan, industrial land price, tourism washrooms, road paving contract and Riverfest approvals
overview: Council voted to keep the Township opted out of retail cannabis storefronts, and asked staff to report back if the Province changes its implementation regulations. A motion to opt in was defeated {{vote:m8}}, and the opt-out was then carried {{vote:m9}}.

Council adopted Official Plan Amendment No. 14, the South Fergus Secondary Plan, and sent it to the County of Wellington for approval {{vote:m13}}. It also delegated authority to staff to change the Elora Rocks agreement, allowing the 2024 payment to be made by December 31, 2024 {{vote:m6}}. Council kept industrial land at $450,000 per acre {{vote:m11}} and awarded the 2024 road asphalting tender for $1,961,641.11 excluding HST {{vote:m15}}.

Other decisions cover public washrooms beside the Elora Fergus Tourism Centre, to be built by a private company and donated to the Township {{vote:m14}}. Council also approved Riverfest Elora's amplified music hours and Municipally Significant Event status {{vote:m3}}, and directed staff to develop a priority registration policy for recreation programs with waitlists {{vote:m10}}. Staff will give a full update on the new Operations Centre on June 10.

decisions.detail: Council will continue to opt out of retail cannabis storefronts and staff will report back if the Province changes implementation regulations {{vote:m9}}.
Council approved application OP04/2023 and adopted Official Plan Amendment No. 14 for submission to the County of Wellington {{vote:m13}}.
Staff were delegated authority to change the agreement, including allowing the 2024 payment to be remitted by December 31, 2024 {{vote:m6}}.

Council authorized an agreement with Kat Florence Canada Company Limited to design and build public washrooms at 10 East Mill Street, with a $25,000 Township budget from the General Capital Reserve {{vote:m14}}.
Tender #18-24 was awarded to Cox Construction Limited at $1,961,641.11, including contingency and excluding HST {{vote:m15}}.
Council maintained the sale price of municipal industrial land at $450,000 per acre {{vote:m11}}.
Staff will develop a Priority Registration Policy benefiting residents for programs with waitlists or registration complaints, and return it for approval {{vote:m10}}.
Council authorized amplified music at Bissell Park on August 16 to 18 and designated the event Municipally Significant {{vote:m3}}.
